findings.F1: The book's loss comes mostly from fees, not from the market's direction. Per hour the position's gross gain is -0.000036 (BTC) and -0.000024 (ETH), against net book returns of -0.000132 and -0.000119. Turnover is 0.13 and 0.11 of allocation per bar, and the 3,838 and 3,861 trades average -0.45% / -0.50% before fees and -0.55% / -0.60% after.
findings.F2: The market's own rise explains almost none of the book's mean daily return of -0.0031 (BTC) and -0.0029 (ETH). That market part is -0.00010 (BTC) and +0.000017 (ETH), so timing is the larger part and it is negative.
findings.F3: The book's worst-quintile days are the coin's strongest up days, with book -0.032 / -0.030 against coin +0.030 / +0.038. Its best-quintile days gain only +0.013 on coin moves of -0.008 / -0.013, so the short book loses more in squeezes than it earns in falls.
findings.F4: The forecast shows no graded effect on the 12-bar excess return. The zero-forecast group gives -0.00016 (t -0.26, n 1437) and the nonzero |forecast| quintiles give -0.0001, +0.0023, -0.0008 and -0.0003 (t between -0.63 and +1.83), with no monotone order.
findings.F5: The largest 72-hour falls (lowest quintile of the 72-hour return) are followed by below-average returns, but only weakly. Over 12 hours the excess is -0.0021 (BTC, t -1.30, n 284) and -0.0038 (ETH, t -1.80); over 24 hours it is -0.0032 (t -0.94) and -0.0072 (t -1.77). The Spearman rank correlation between the 72-hour return and the next 24 hours is about 0.02 and -0.01.
findings.F6: Volatility level, the ratio of recent to longer volatility, the 168-hour return, weekday and hour of day produce no group that stands out from about 150 cells. The largest are hour 19 at t +1.94 (BTC) and +1.56 (ETH), and Thursday at -1.69 (BTC) and -0.99 (ETH), which is in line with chance for this many cells.

no_ideas: Every pattern in the bars that the idea does not explain stays below what chance produces across the roughly 150 cells examined: weakest-72-hour continuation peaks at t -1.8, hour 19 at +1.9, and volatility and weekday splits are smaller. The book's failure is explained by fees and short-squeeze losses inherent to the tested idea (F1–F3), so no finding is strong enough to support a new idea.
